results.title: Mars attacks! [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Tim Burton, Larry Franco and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: Science fiction and cult movie fans will warm to Tim Burton’s distinct brand of humour in this sci-fi spoof where, once again, Earth is invaded by martians. These mean green invaders from the Red Planet have slimey humungous brains, are armed with Instr-ray guns, and are cinematically supported by state-of-the-art special effects. The stars that shine here include Jack Nicholson (in a dual role), Glenn Close, Annette Bening, Pierce Brosnan, Danny DeVito, plus many more notable cameos (including one by Tom Jones).

results.title: The Searchers [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: John Ford, Merian C. Cooper and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: Ethan Edwards (John Wayne) resolves to find his niece, abducted by Indians at the close of the Civil War. It is an odyssey which takes five years, by the end of which he plans to take revenge on the Indians for the friends and family he has lost. John Ford used sumptuous Monument Valley as a background for this his most poetic and complex western. Cast includes Vera Miles and a young Natalie Wood. Based on a novel by Alan Le May. A documentary written and directed by Nick Redman entitled, “A Turning of the earth: John Ford, John Wayne and ‘The Searchers’”, featuring outtakes, home movies and the original theatrical trailer precedes the film. Introduced by Patrick Wayne.

results.title: The Wild bunch [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Sam Peckinpah, Phil Feldman and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: In 1913, a gang known as “The Wild Bunch”, rode into a Texas border town disguised as U.S. soldiers. Silently they entered the railroad office and robbed it. Perched on the rooftops above was a ring of hired gunmen waiting for their prey. When the gang emerged they opened fire. An exciting, provocative and influential film that breathed new life into Westerns, it brings together an all-star cast of fine actors at the peak of their talents to play the band of magnificent losers in a dying, lawless West. A documentary, “The Wild Bunch: an album in montage”, as well as a new introduction by Ernest Borgnine precedes the movie.

results.title: Unforgiven [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Clint Eastwood, Malpaso Company and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: Clint Eastwood’s film is an exciting modern classic that rode off with four 1992 Academy Awards including Best Picture and Director. Eastwood and Morgan Freeman play retired down-on-their-luck outlaws who pick up their guns one last time to collect a bounty offered by the vengeful prostitutes of the remote Wyoming town of Big Whiskey. Richard Harris is an ill-fated interloper, a colourful killer for hire called English Bob. Gene Hackman is the sly and brutal local sheriff whose brand of law enforcement ranges from unconventional to ruthless. Big trouble is coming to Big Whiskey.

results.title: Enter the dragon [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Robert Clouse, Paul Heller, Fred Weintraub, Concorde Productions and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: One of the biggest martial arts epics ever filmed. Bruce Lee, determined to avenge the murder of his sister, enters the island fortress of crime warlord Han. Lee staged his own fighting sequences in the movie and the sequences are thrilling in their timing and execution. ‘Enter the dragon’ was Lee’s last film and his untimely death at a young age, a few weeks after the film’s completion had made this a landmark film of its genre.

results.title: Romance on the high seas = It's magic
results.creator_credit: Michael Curtiz, Alex Gottlieb and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: Elvira and Michael Kent (Janis Paige and Don De Fore) are about to celebrate their third anniversary, however for the third year in a row, Michael can’t make it. Elvira has always suspected her husband of being a philanderer, so decides to tell her husband that she’s going away on their anniversary cruise to South America without him, while secretly staying behind and spying on him from an apartment opposite his work. When there’s a mix up at the drugstore between Elvira’s passport and that of nightclub singer Georgia Garrett (Doris Day), the plan begins to take shape. Georgia has never travelled before, and jumps at the opportunity to take an all expenses paid cruise; the only hitch is she has to pretend she’s Lady Elvira Kent. Michael is as suspicious as his wife when it comes to fidelity, and he is surprised by her lack of concern about him not coming on the cruise. Instead of hiring someone to impersonate him, Michael hires personal detective Peter Virgil (Jack Carson) to go on the cruise and keep an eye on his wife. Peter and Georgia are drawn together and fall in love but are held back by their loyalty to the people who have hired them. The film culminates in the carnival city of Rio, where Georgia, Peter, the real Mr and Mrs Kent, and Georgia’s friend who wants to marry her are all in the same hotel, where all will be revealed. This was Doris Day’s first film role.

results.title: Scaramouche
results.creator_credit: George Sidney, Carey Wilson and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer
results.brief_description: This version of Rafael Sabatini’s swashbuckler stars Stewart Granger as Andre Moreau, an 18th century French nobleman who disguises himself as an actor to revenge the death of his brother at the hands of a wicked marquis. Challenged to a sword fight by the marquis, Moreau takes refuge in a theatrical troupe, posing as the clown - Scaramouche. Being in disguise provides Moreau with the time to take fencing lessons from swordmaster Doutreval (John Dehner), as well as romancing his leading lady, Lenore (Eleanor Parker). When Moreau/Scaramouche has learnt all there is to know about fencing, it’s time to face his adversary, and there are a few surprises in store too that have nothing to do with duelling. This remake credits itself as containing the longest sword fight in cinema history. Cast also includes Janet Leigh and Mel Ferrer.

results.title: Darby's rangers = The Young invaders
results.creator_credit: William Wellman, Martin Rackin and Warner Bros Pictures
results.brief_description: In his first starring film role James Garner plays Colonel William Darby, an Army man in charge of organizing a group of rangers to be deployed in activities in Italy and Northern Africa. The film is chiefly presented in two parts - the preparation of the rangers, and their deployment in live action. Cast includes Etchika Choureau, Jack Warden and Edward Byrnes.

results.title: Empire of the sun [Widescreen]
results.creator_credit: Steven Spielberg, Frank Marshall, Kathleen Kennedy, Amblin Entertainment and Robert Shapiro
results.brief_description: Jim Graham, a young Briton living a comfortable life in Shanghai, is separated from his parents following the Japanese invasion of China at the start of World War II. The separation leads to Jim being caught in an internment camp where he has to fend for himself. Cast includes John Malkovich, Christian Bale, Miranda Richardson and Nigel Havers. Based on the autobiographical novel by J. G. Ballard.

results.title: Tribute to a bad man
results.creator_credit: Robert Wise, Sam Zimbalist and Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer
results.brief_description: James Cagney stars as a no-nonsense land baron Jeremy Rodock, who plays by his own rules, his own sense of justice and his own code of honour. Young cowhand Steve Miller (Don Dubbins) learns the hard way what it mean’s to incur Rodock’s wrath when he falls in love with the beautiful Jocasta Constantine (Irene Papas), whom Rodock considers his property. Through the example of the even-tempered Miller, however, Rodock rediscovers his own essential humanity. This excellent adaptation of Jack Schaefer’s short story features early screen appearances by Vic Morrow and Lee Van Cleef.
